principle_violations.reason: The code violates the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle in several places. The calculation of the amounts (this_amount) and the bonus points (volume_credits) contains repetitive logic for different theatre performance types. In addition, the currency formatting is performed several times in the code and the output statement.
principle_violations.suggestion: The repetitive code parts should be outsourced to separate functions: A function for calculating the amounts (calculate_amount), a function for calculating the bonus points (calculate_volume_credits), a central function for currency conversion and formatting and a separate class for the different performance types with their specific calculation logic

principle_violations.reason: This code violates the Single Responsibility Principle because the statement method class is responsible for calculating the amount and the volume_credits, the currency and the output statement
principle_violations.suggestion: The code parts should be outsourced to separate functions: A function for calculating the amounts (calculate_amount), a function for calculating the volume credits (calculate_volume_credits), a function for currency formatting and a function for generating the output statement

principle_violations.reason: This current statement method violates the Open/Closed Principle, as the existing code would have to be modified for each new play types.
principle_violations.suggestion: In order to comply with the open-closed principle, play types should be implemented with an abstract base class (e.g. PerformanceType). Each play types implement the methods of the performanceType (e.g. TragedyPerformance, ComedyPerformance).
